title: Refugees and the Hijra
hookLine: the Prophet's own leaving of home, and the people on the roads today

cards: Two men in a cave, with the people hunting them somewhere outside. Outside is the city they grew up in, and it no longer wants them. One of them is afraid.
The other says, in Pickthall's translation of the Qur'an: "Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us."

The two are the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his friend Abu Bakr, and the journey is the Hijra, the leaving of Mecca for Medina. A story of the past, and of the people on the roads right now.

teach.b: Hijra is the Arabic word for this leaving. It was not a holiday. The Qur'an, in the chapter called Exile, speaks of the migrants as poor, driven out from their homes and their belongings.
Tradition says the Muslim calendar counts its years from this leaving. Now look at who met them.
The people of Medina, the Ansar, the helpers, took the newcomers into their homes, and the next verse of that chapter praises them.
In Pickthall's words, they "prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot." Fugitives is Pickthall's word for the migrants. Al-Bukhari keeps a scene from those days.

teach.h: SHOW ME THE WAY TO THE MARKET.
teach.b: One of the helpers, Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', was paired as a brother with one of the newcomers, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and offered him half of everything he owned. 'Abd al-Rahman thanked him and said, in paraphrase: just show me the way to the market.
A welcome on one side. Dignity on the other.
The Qur'an also speaks of someone outside the faith who asks for protection. Surah nine says that if one of the idolaters seeks protection, he is to be protected and then escorted somewhere safe.

teach.h: THEY PREFER THE FUGITIVES ABOVE THEMSELVES.
teach.b: So when Muslims today look at families crossing borders with what they can carry, some see the Hijra again: a Prophet who was himself once a refugee, and a city that made room. The mirror works both ways.
It asks what it is to flee, and what it is to be the Ansar.

how: Some Muslim charities and mosques support refugees, and some teachers point to the Hijra and to the Ansar of Medina, who took the migrants into their homes, when they speak about welcoming people who have fled.

games.q: what does “refugees and the hijra” mean?
o: the yearly holiday marking the Prophet's night journey to Jerusalem
a pilgrimage every Muslim makes to Medina once in a lifetime
the Prophet's forced leaving of Mecca, mirrored in those fleeing today

games.q: the Hijra and the welcome — tap the pairs.
p: in the cave with the Prophet
offered half of what he owned
show me the way to the market

s: in 9:40, Abu Bakr tells the Prophet 'Grieve not'
the verse has the Prophet say it to his companion in the cave: "Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us."
the Qur'an praises the Ansar for preferring the migrants above themselves
"prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot" (59:9, Pickthall).
'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf accepted half of Sa'd's wealth
he thanked him and asked to be shown the way to the market.

games.q: you've just arrived in Medina with almost nothing. your new brother from the Ansar offers you half of everything he owns. what do you say?
o: thank him, and ask the way to the market.
refuse to speak to him out of pride.
games.why: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf thanked Sa'd and asked to be shown the market. a generous welcome, and a newcomer who wanted to stand on his own feet.

practice: Think of a time you left somewhere, a home, a school, a country, a job: what did you carry, and who met you on the other side, or didn't?
Then think of someone, anywhere, who left home this year with no choice and arrived with very little, and hold them for a while; you don't need a name.
If you pray, remember them in your prayers; if you don't, simply keep them in mind.

wordCard.voice: Refugees and the Hijra. The Prophet's forced leaving of Mecca, the welcome in Medina, and the mirror it holds up to people fleeing home today. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a leaving or migration; above all, the Prophet's move from Mecca to Medina.

carryVoice: Your line: the hijra today. Every leaving needs someone waiting. Until tomorrow.
